7 Research Integrity Advisors (RIAs)
(A). Research Integrity Advisor means members of the University Community who are
appointed to provide advice about the responsible conduct of research and the University
processes for dealing with allegations of Research Misconduct.
(B). The University, in accordance to the Research Code, will —
(1). appoint Research Integrity Advisors to assist Researchers in addressing ethical and
procedural issues in the design and conduct of their Research; and
(2). appoint Research Integrity Advisors who are experienced Researchers with a good
knowledge and understanding of accepted practices in Research who actively promote
the University’s commitment to the responsible conduct of Research.

case_summary.review_route_explanation: Research misconduct and authorship/governance breaches are handled under N055 section 17(D), with HDR decisions reviewable under N046.

version_evidence_location.text: Approval Date 08 December 2022 Administrator(s) AD Research Operations

case_summary.critical_risk_criterion: Authorised, safe execution, meaningful human intervention and accountable research responsibility.
case_summary.critical_gap_explanation: Under Protocol v1.1 (adopted after preliminary review on 2026-11-15), while N055 enforces human authorship accountability, UWA lacks operational authorisation, safety-gating, and meaningful human-intervention controls between AI-generated procedures and physical laboratory or computational execution.
case_summary.case_note: UWA Research Integrity Policy N055 requires substantial human intellectual contribution, final publication approval, and compliance with ethics, equipment, and safety rules, while N071 covers automated digital agents. However, UWA lacks operational procedures and human-intervention gates governing autonomous multi-agent AI execution of laboratory or computational actions, leaving a critical gap. Note that Protocol v1.1 critical-risk criteria were adopted after preliminary review.
